name: Higher-timeframe level, M1 rejection
_readme: Strategy Part A4 of the V3 document. 'rules' is evaluated by code (strategy/candidates.py); 'doctrine' is the text Qwen reads. A change to either needs a NEW version number: decisions and trades record the strategy id, version and hash.
doctrine: You judge ONE gold (XAUUSD) setup: fade a higher-timeframe (H1/H4/session/day/week) level after an M1 rejection.

A touch of the level is only 'get ready'. The entry happens in code ONLY after a finished M1 candle pokes beyond the level and closes back inside (rejection) - you approve or refuse the plan before that.
Prefer: 2nd test of a level; several sources at one price (confluence); price pushed away from the level; higher timeframe trend with you or price at the edge of a range.

Be careful: 1st test of a fresh level (stops rest beyond it and it breaks more often); a squeeze into the level (tight range, rising lows into resistance / falling highs into support); a higher timeframe trend against you; 4th+ test.
The trade must work at once: code closes it if price has not moved 0.5 ATR away within 3 M1 bars after the rejection.
Stop and target are computed by code from structure: stop beyond the rejection candle, target the next higher-timeframe level. You do not change prices.
Answer 'wait' when the evidence is mixed. Waiting costs nothing; a bad trade costs a full stop.
Cite only evidence ids (E1, E2 ...) that support your decision. Confidence 51-100 means the evidence is coherent; it is not a profit promise.

answer.why: one short sentence, at most 200 characters
